claims.text: Conventional hot-dip aluminum plating parts are typically made from steels or traditional alloys.
Conventional dipping and plating parts suffer rapid dissolution or erosion in molten aluminum.
Manufacturing hot-dip aluminum plating components from a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy will reduce erosion relative to conventional materials.
Tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys can possess high strength at elevated temperature.
Other refractory elements can be included to stabilize the alloy structure at high temperatures.
The proposed RHEA microstructure is stable at high temperatures.
The proposed RHEA forms a continuous protective oxide layer during service.
The protective oxide layer acts as a diffusion barrier.
A tungsten-based RHEA forms a stable alumina-based or other dense refractory oxide at hot-dip aluminum plating temperatures.
The proposed oxide layer reduces chemical attack by molten aluminum.
Reduced chemical attack by molten aluminum inhibits component erosion.
Tungsten-based RHEA components will show significantly lower weight loss or material degradation over extended service than conventional components.
Lower erosion of tungsten-based RHEA components will extend equipment service life.
Protective performance may diminish if temperature or mechanical loading causes the oxide layer to degrade or spall.
Extreme stress, thermal cycling, or unforeseen processing conditions may diminish the alloy's protective performance.
Tungsten-based refractory alloys offer oxidation resistance.
The long-term interaction of the proposed tungsten-based RHEA with liquid aluminum has not been validated under industrial plating conditions.
The cited tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy achieves a yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 degrees Celsius.
